templates.name: Claim submitted returns a business response (not a 500)
templates.expected: HTTP 200 with a real claim_id / adjudication result in the body — an error page or internal_server_error is a FAIL even if the pod is green
templates.hint: This is the front half of the success bar. Use the partner-shaped payload, not a health check.

templates.name: Settlement/remittance import runs end-to-end
templates.command: kubectl -n <ns> create job --from=cronjob/<settlement-import> dr-test-import && kubectl logs -f job/dr-test-import
templates.expected: Import completes; new rows visible in the recovered remittance database
templates.hint: The back half of the success bar. Batch paths fail differently from request paths — test both.

templates.name: Auth flow works against recovered identity provider
templates.expected: Valid token issued and accepted by a protected endpoint
templates.hint: Identity pools / authorizers are region-bound more often than teams expect.

templates.name: Async queue consumers drain a test message
templates.command: aws sqs send-message --queue-url <recovered-queue-url> --message-body @test-message.json && watch queue depth
templates.expected: Message consumed within normal latency; downstream side effect observed
templates.hint: Consumers that started before the queue existed may be wedged — check consumer age vs queue age.

templates.name: Database freshness query (measures RPA)
templates.expected: Age at T0 within the recovery-point window — record the number as measured RPA
templates.hint: Run against every Tier-0 database; the worst number is the honest RPA.

templates.name: Secrets resolution clean (secrets-init or equivalent)
templates.expected: Zero resolution errors; every logical name resolves in the recovery region
templates.hint: The most common test-killer. Check BEFORE blaming the app.

templates.name: Images pulled from recovery-region registry
templates.expected: Every image host is the recovery-region registry — zero references to the primary region
templates.hint: A pod pulling cross-region from the 'dead' primary passes the test and fails the disaster.

templates.name: Edge reachable via direct endpoint + Host header (no DNS change)
templates.expected: HTTP 200 from recovered backends through the recovered edge chain
templates.hint: Proves L5 without touching public DNS — the Phase-1 way to test the front door.

templates.name: Scheduled report/batch job generates output
templates.expected: Report written to the recovered bucket with today's date
templates.hint: Report jobs find region-bound bucket names and stale IAM faster than anything else.

templates.name: Partner webhook received by recovered stack
templates.command: Ask partner (or webhook simulator) to POST to the direct recovery endpoint
templates.expected: Webhook accepted, signature verified, downstream processing observed
templates.hint: Inbound partner traffic exercises authorizers and allowlists that outbound tests miss.

templates.name: Cache rebuild path works cold
templates.command: redis-cli -h <recovered-redis> dbsize; then exercise an app path that populates it
templates.expected: App serves correctly (if slower) with a cold cache; cache fills as traffic flows
templates.hint: Caches are usually rebuilt, not restored — prove the app tolerates empty.

templates.name: Outbound third-party call succeeds from recovery egress
templates.command: From a recovered pod: curl -s <partner-api-endpoint>/ping (or the app's own outbound health probe)
templates.expected: Partner endpoint answers — proves egress routing, NAT, and any partner allowlist
templates.hint: If the partner allowlists source IPs, this fails until recovery egress IPs are registered.

templates.name: Observability shows the recovery stack
templates.command: Open the DR dashboard; confirm metrics/logs flowing from recovery-region workloads
templates.expected: Dashboards populated with live recovery-region data — the runbook gates are readable
templates.hint: If you can't see it, you can't verify it; a blind recovery passes on vibes.
